title: Heuristic edge fallback and budgeted shedding for multi-region routing
creator: Ravi Kapoor
description: Problem: During cross-region load spikes and partial datacenter degradations we need routing that preserves user-visible SLOs while minimizing wholesale capacity overprovisioning. Current region steering is binary (pin or failover) and does not take short-term capacity fluctuations and tenant SLO tiers into account. This ticket proposes a heuristic-driven edge fallback and budgeted shedding policy that blends latency-based routing, ephemeral geo-pinning, and per-tenant capacity credits to provide graceful, observable degradation with predictable SLO impact.
background_and_motivation: We frequently see two classes of failure: (1) transient latency spikes in a single region where hedging to distant regions improves P99 but costs tokens and increases tail variance; (2) capacity shortages where naive failover creates hot cold spots and cascades into other regions. Product asks for predictable SLO exposure per-customer (hosted vs dedicated) and for Console to show expected token-cost delta for routing decisions. Ops needs circuit breaker windows and a fast rollback knob.
design_notes: Introduce a per-request routing decision vector: {latency_estimate, region_capacity_score, customer_slo_tier, budget_credits, affinity_score}.
Capacity score computed from moving window of allocator metrics (usable_gpus, queued_requests, avg_inflight_tokens) normalized per-region and per-instance type.

Budgeted shedding: assign each customer a short-term capacity credit pool (tokens/sec equivalent) that is consumed when requests are routed to non-preferred regions or when served with lower-cost quantized model variants. Credits recharge slowly and are exposed in Console. Dedicated customers can opt-out or set custom policies.

Soft circuit breakers: instead of hard drop, systems apply progressive throttling rates (10%, 30%, 60%) with exponential backoff and a thaw period. Breakers are gated by region_capacity_score and SLO burn rate.

Ephemeral geo-pinning: prefer primary region for low-latency requests if affinity_score > threshold, otherwise consider secondary regions when latency_estimate for primary exceeds SLO delta or capacity_score < low-watermark.
Probing lane: maintain a small percentage (default 1%) of traffic routed to candidate regions for capacity health checks and to prime caches (KV/prefix), avoiding cold-start P99 blowups on failover.

Fallback policy: implement a three-tier fallback matrix: prefer same-region low-cost variants -> nearest-region compatible model -> global fallthrough with aggressive batching and cache-hints. Each step annotated with expected latency and token-cost delta for Console display.
Observability: add routing_decision event with all vector components and explainability tags; surface per-customer SLO burn and budget credit state in Console and in incident dashboards.
Rollout: feature flag gating per-account; start with internal traffic, then controlled customer cohort, then global.

Trade-offs: heuristics are simple to implement and interpretable but may not be globally optimal; a future ML-based router could replace the heuristic layer after stable metrics are gathered. Budget credits add bookkeeping and edge state; keep default conservative values to avoid frequent customer confusion.
acceptance_criteria: Routing decision vector is computed in the edge tier and recorded in traces for 100% of routed requests behind feature flag.
Per-region capacity_score and probing lane health metrics are emitted every 10s and visible in Console graphs.
Budget credit accounting is implemented for hosted customers with default recharge/decay parameters, and Console shows current credit balance per-customer.
Soft circuit breaker throttling actions are reversible via admin knob and have hysteresis to prevent flip-flopping.
End-to-end canary: internal traffic shows reduced P99 during simulated single-region latencies and graceful degradation under synthetic capacity limits (test harness attached).
Performance: additional latency for routing decision should be < 1ms p50 and < 2ms p99 in edge path.
Playbook: runbook added to Confluence describing how to interpret budget credit exhaustion and how to trigger immediate rollback.
Unit/Integration tests and a staged rollout are completed and approved by SRE and Runtime PM.
Console UX showing expected token-cost delta for fallback steps is implemented for the default customer cohort.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike + proto): 4d spike to implement decision vector schema, capacity_score aggregation, and minimal probing lane. Add trace/event attrs. (Ravi + Maya)
Phase 2 (budgeting + soft breakers): 6d implement per-customer credit pool and progressive throttling; expose admin rollbacks and telemetry. (Maya, backend team)
Phase 3 (console + rollout): 4d Console changes to surface credits and predicted cost delta, plus UX for per-customer opt-out. Controlled rollout with feature flag. (Frontend/PM)
Phase 4 (hardening): 3d tuning of thresholds, default parameters, and adding e2e tests in stress harness. (SRE)
Total estimate: 17d (matches cycle estimate 8 story points mapped to team velocity)
testing_plan: Unit tests for capacity_score calculator and budget credit state transitions.
Integration tests: emulated multi-region deployment with synthetic latencies and capacity constraints; assert SLO burn rates and routing decisions.
Chaos tests: inject region-level packet loss and disk pressure while ensuring probing lane avoids cold-cache P99 spikes.
Load tests: ramp to 3x normal qps and verify soft circuit breakers throttle according to policy without cascading failures.
Canary: internal traffic -> small external cohort (5 customers) -> progressive ramp to 25% accounts over 2 weeks.
rollout_plan: Feature flag default: off for hosted customers; on for internal and staging clusters.
Enable for a pilot cohort selected by traffic patterns (low burstiness) and notify Customer Success teams.
Monitor SLO burn, token-cost delta, and customer feedback for 72h before a wider rollout.
Provide emergency rollback flag and runbook; incident channel #routing-fallback and playbook reference linked.
Post-rollout: collect metrics for 14 days and iterate thresholds.
dependencies: ENG-53120 (quantized-fallthrough-routing) - compatibility with model variant selection
